me_east_side.blurb: East Side is a section of the Ten Degree Wall in western Maine, found by walking along the cliff base past the Friction Slabs. Walls run up to roughly 100 feet and are split by a number of cracks, so most of the fifteen routes here are traditional lines with just two bolted ones. Difficulty starts around 5.7 and tops out in the low 5.12 range, though the bulk of the climbing sits between 5.9 and 5.11, which suits a leader who is comfortable on moderate-to-hard crack and face climbing. Bring a full trad rack and expect a quieter day than at the better-known sections of the wall.

me_left_wall.blurb: The Left Wall is one of the sections of Great Head, the sea cliff on the Acadia coast of Maine, and a trail leads right to its base. Unlike much of Great Head, this wall depends little on the tide. The fifteen routes are mostly traditional, with several set up as top-ropes and a single bolted line. Grades begin around 5.6 and run through the 5.10s and 5.11s up to a couple of routes in the 5.13 range, so there is a good mix of approachable leads and hard test pieces. A fair choice for a coastal day when you want single-pitch trad.

me_07_pink_quarry.blurb: Pink Quarry is a small bouldering zone inside Clifford Park, the city park in Biddeford, reached by following the pink trail soon after it splits away from the Black Loop. The fourteen problems lean toward easy slab and low-to-the-ground climbing, with plenty from VB to V2, a handful of V3 and V4 problems, and one standout project-level problem far harder than anything else. That spread makes it a good spot for beginners and mixed groups. Landings on a few problems are poor, so bring pads and spot carefully. The park's quarry history leaves blocky granite slabs scattered through the woods.

_expect.name: Chimney Pond ("South") Basin - Summer Rock Routes

me_01_chimney_pond_south_basin_summer_ro.blurb: The South Basin is the cirque of cliffs above Chimney Pond on Katahdin, deep in Baxter State Park, and it holds the region's serious alpine rock. All fourteen routes here are traditional, and many are long multi-pitch outings, some running to ten pitches or more. Grades span from 5.5 up to 5.10, with the largest share around 5.7. Expect a wilderness day: the hike in from Roaring Brook is about three miles to the pond before you even start toward the base, and bolts are discouraged, so climbs rely on natural protection. Plan on summer conditions and an early start.

me_fletchers_bluff.blurb: Fletchers Bluff is one of the four main roped crags of Clifton Crags, in the hills east of Bangor. It is a big, complicated cliff band in a quiet setting that sees little traffic, with slabs, roofs and cracks of various sizes. Nearly all of the fourteen routes are bolted sport lines, and the Sundog Wall on the right end holds the best-known ones. Climbing is hard-leaning: it starts around 5.10, most routes fall in the 5.11 to 5.12 range, and there is at least one 5.13. This is a destination for climbers comfortable on steeper sport routes rather than for beginners.

me_02_the_verticals.blurb: The Verticals is a short, compact cliff in the Camden Hills, tucked just left of Barrett's Cove Cliff above Camden. Despite its small size it packs in fourteen routes, a mix of bolted sport lines and some trad, a few of which can also be top-roped. The climbing is steep and technical, on small holds, where footwork and precise movement count for more than raw strength, and it is a popular place to learn steeper rock. Grades range from 5.7 up to a single 5.12, with most routes between 5.9 and 5.11. Expect a scramble over uneven ground near the base.

me_main_face.blurb: The Main Face sits near the middle of Big Chick Hill, one of the Clifton Crags east of Bangor, to the right of Tower Gully. It is known for the longest and best slab climbing in the Clifton area, and several routes run two or three pitches. Of the fourteen routes, more than half are traditional and the rest are bolted. Grades go from 5.5 to 5.11, though the great majority fall between 5.7 and 5.9, making it a friendly face for moderate leaders working up to longer climbs. A steep, brushy gully on the right side gives an alternative way up or down.
